## Issue #80 Software Project Request Requirements

Issue [#80](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/80) reports that
an Owlbear/D&D extension request for HP, Protection/Resistance mitigation, and
cooldown tracking returned `intent: unknown`. The maintainer asked for a
generalization across similar tasks instead of a memoized prompt answer, and
then clarified that the first step must formalize the message into Links
Notation meaning before deriving reasoning and plan steps.

| ID | Requirement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R156 | Open-ended requests to build or write a software artifact (extension, plugin, bot, app, service, website, or tool) must route to a typed software-project intent instead of `unknown`. | Implemented by `try_software_project_request` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/software_project.rs`, mirrored by `trySoftwareProjectRequest` in `js/worker/formal_ai_worker.js`, and registered in `data/seed/intent-routing.lino`. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/formal_ai.rs` (`software_project_request_returns_reviewable_plan`, `software_project_variations_do_not_return_unknown`) and, for the worker twin, by `rust/tests/web/issue-0080-software-project.test.mjs`. |
| R157 | The first response must formalize the user text into a reviewable Links Notation meaning record before producing project steps. | Implemented by the software-project meaning parser and `software_project_request` Links Notation block rendered in Rust and browser responses. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/software_project.rs` (`software_project_plan_exposes_requirement_graph_and_approval_preferences`) and, byte for byte against the Rust plans, by `rust/tests/web/issue-0080-software-project.test.mjs`. |
| R158 | The meaning record must model the task as a graph of requirements and subtasks, grouped by general categories instead of by one-off memorized prompts. | Implemented by requirement extraction, category assignment, subtask derivation, `Requirement model`, and `Subtasks` sections in Rust and browser responses. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/software_project.rs` (`software_project_plan_exposes_requirement_graph_and_approval_preferences`, `software_project_dialogue_examples_formalize_plan_then_implement_after_approval`) and by `rust/tests/web/issue-0080-software-project.test.mjs`. |
| R159 | The response must derive deep reasoning steps and a detailed implementation plan from the meaning record, then wait for user approval before converting the plan into code, scripts, manual instructions, or execution steps. | Implemented by the plan response asking for `approve plan`, by the approval follow-up handler that uses the prior user request and assistant plan, and by explicit delivery-mode/approval-gate fields. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/software_project.rs` (`software_project_dialogue_examples_formalize_plan_then_implement_after_approval`, `software_project_followup_requires_an_active_plan`) and by `rust/tests/web/issue-0080-software-project.test.mjs`. |

| R162 | The browser demo must handle the reported Owlbear prompt and generalized software-project prompts without showing the unknown-intent fallback. | Implemented and covered by `software_project_request_returns_reviewable_plan` (`rust/tests/unit/formal_ai.rs`), `software_project_variations_do_not_return_unknown`, the full dialogue matrix, and the Playwright regression `Owlbear extension request returns a software project plan`; the browser worker returns the Rust plan byte for byte in `rust/tests/web/issue-0080-software-project.test.mjs`. |

supported subset deterministic, reviewable, and permission-gated.

requires the browser worker to derive the same synthesis, numeric, program,
and text answers as the Rust core for the E28-E31 work, while keeping Rust/WASM
as the owner of shared primitives and JavaScript as browser glue.

| ID | Requirement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R246 | Browser-worker synthesis prompts must route to typed derived intents instead of `unknown` or legacy write-program templates. | Implemented by `tryLinkNativeSynthesis`, `tryProgramSynthesis`, and `tryTextManipulation` in `js/worker/formal_ai_worker.js`, inserted ahead of the legacy arithmetic/write-program fallbacks. |
| R247 | Rust and browser parity must be checked from a shared fixture that covers algebra substitution, renumbered remainder-sale arithmetic, object counting with a distractor, unseen Python synthesis, and chained text manipulation. | Covered by `data/parity/cross-runtime-synthesis.json`, `shared_cross_runtime_synthesis_fixture_matches_rust_solver`, and `rust/tests/e2e/tests/issue-327.spec.js`. |
| R248 | Anti-memorization checks must hold on the browser side for renumbered numeric answers, distractor counts, and unseen synthesized programs. | Implemented: The shared fixture includes forbidden fragments such as `18`, `4`, and `legacy_intent`; the browser e2e asserts they do not appear in rendered answers and checks semantic forbidden evidence for legacy routes. |
| R249 | WASM must remain the bridge for shared primitives while JS performs browser-only composition and glue. | Delivered: browser synthesis delegates arithmetic evaluation and stable id creation through `wasmEvaluateArithmetic` and `wasmStableId` when available, with JS fallbacks only for no-WASM compatibility. |

## Issue #349 Reverse-Sort Program Modification Roadmap

Issue [#349](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/349) reported a
multi-turn Russian coding dialog where the assistant wrote a Rust program,
successfully modified it to accept a path argument, then answered the next
program-modification follow-up with `intent: unknown` instead of reversing the
sort order. The roadmap split that defect into issues
[#355](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/355) through
[#365](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/365). The final epic
[#365](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/365) records that
issues #355-#364 are closed and merged, and that the #349 dialog is green in the
Rust core, browser worker, diagnostics surface, and coding-modification
benchmark.

| ID | Requirement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R256 | The issue #349 reverse-sort follow-up must route to a real program-modification answer instead of `unknown`. | Implemented by `rust/tests/integration/issue_349_reverse_sort.rs::issue_349_reverse_sort_follow_up_must_not_be_unknown`: the fifth turn routes to `write_program`, preserves the path-argument edit, and emits reverse-sort code. |
| R257 | Bare program-result follow-ups must bind to the active program artifact before program lowering. | Implemented by the active-program coreference flow added for #357 and covered by `rust/tests/unit/specification/code_generation_coreference.rs`; the #349 trace records `referent=active_program_artifact task=list_files_arg language=rust`. |
| R258 | Program modifiers must compose from data instead of a one-off `path_argument` allowlist. | Implemented by the generalized modifier model in `rust/src/program_plan.rs`, `rust/src/rule_synthesis.rs`, `data/seed/operation-vocabulary.lino`, and `data/seed/program-plan-rules.lino`; tests cover `path_argument` plus `reverse_sort` composition into `list_files_arg_reverse_sort`. Covered by `rust/tests/unit/issue_936_substitution_compiler.rs`. |
| R259 | Unknown program follow-ups must attempt reasoned rule construction before reporting failure. | Implemented by the #359 rule-construction path and covered across supported prompt languages by `rust/tests/unit/specification/code_generation_program_modifiers.rs` and the #349 diagnostics test. |
| R260 | The write-program reasoning chain must be inspectable and diagnostics must remain default off. | Implemented by `SolverConfig::diagnostic_mode`, `rust/tests/integration/issue_349_reverse_sort.rs::issue_349_diagnostic_mode_emits_full_turn_5_reasoning_chain`, and browser e2e coverage in `rust/tests/e2e/tests/issue-360.spec.js`. |
| R261 | The #349 behavior must be consistent across the Rust core and browser worker. | Implemented by `experiments/issue-361-cross-runtime-parity.mjs`, which verifies the browser-worker mirror handles the same turn-5 follow-up, trace, and no-active-program guard as the Rust core. | R265 | The issue #349 child issues and their final status must remain auditable from repository documentation. | Implemented by `docs/case-studies/issue-365/README.md` and the Issue #349 section in `ROADMAP.md`, which map #355-#365 to their closing PRs and verification evidence. ## Issue #468 Agentic-Coding Mode

Issue [#468](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/468) — title
*"Our system should be able to solve such tasks in agentic mode"* — is reframed by
the maintainer comment: the text-formalization protocol in the issue body (Igor
Martynov's *Formal protocol for translating texts into a knowledge base*, with
«Сказка о рыбаке и рыбке» as the canonical input) is **an example task** the system
should solve from the prompt, and the **core task** is the agentic capability —
*"our Formal AI is able to solve the task in agentic coding mode … call all the
tools from any agentic CLI, understand errors from tools … web fetch and web
search"*. Per the comment the project must also collect the issue data, produce a
deep case study with online research, enumerate every requirement, and propose
per-requirement solution plans surveying existing components. Two constraints bind:
the maintainer's *everything is a link* position means the example task's knowledge
base is emitted directly in Links Notation (the meta-language already in the code
base), not as typed-struct entities/ontologies; and external CLIs (`claude`,
`codex`) are pointed *at* the server, never wired *into* the Formal AI engine. The
work lands in PR [#469](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/469).

| ID | Requirement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R306 | The application must provide a capability to solve the example task — translating texts into a knowledge base following the formal protocol, with «Сказка о рыбаке и рыбке» as the canonical input. | Implemented by `formalize_text_to_links` (`rust/src/agentic_coding/formalize.rs`), which drives the example task end to end; surfaced through `formal-ai agent` (`rust/src/main.rs`) and re-exported from `rust/src/agentic_coding/mod.rs`. |
| R307 | The nine protocol primitives must be realized: Concept, Entity, Predicate, Assertion, Procedure, Context, Temporal, Modal, Annotation (the article's full field set is the spec). | Implemented as the nine Links Notation record kinds `PRIMITIVE_KINDS` (`rust/src/agentic_coding/formalize.rs`), each emitted as a record by the formalizer; for the canonical synopsis `summary.covers_all_nine()` is `true`, pinned in `rust/tests/unit/agentic_coding.rs`. The formalizer populates the deterministically-extractable field subset; the full article field set is captured in `docs/case-studies/issue-468/raw-data/article-summary.md`. |
| R308 | The representation must be assertion-centric — assertions are the units of search, inference, and aggregation. | Implemented: each fact is one atomic `assertion` record whose `subject`/`predicate`/`object` associations are links into the entity/predicate/concept catalogue and whose qualifiers are ordinary associations; search/inference/aggregation run over that emitted Links Notation store with the crate's general links tooling rather than a bespoke query engine. |
| R309 | The operational format must stay distinct from an ontology schema: assertions + procedures + modality + provenance carry the facts, while Concept/Predicate declarations remain a fact-free reference directory. | Implemented by a structural `source` vs `provenance` distinction: text-derived assertions carry `provenance "<doc>@<start>:<end>"`, while lexicon-sourced catalogue records (concept/procedure/context) are tagged `source "lexicon:<doc>"`, keeping the reference directory separable from the facts without a schema layer. |
| R310 | Each assertion must carry the protocol's qualifiers: modality, time, context, confidence, and provenance. | Implemented: `assertion` records carry optional `time`/`modal`/`context` associations plus `annotation` + `provenance`; the `temporal` and `modal` primitives (the latter with a `degree`) are emitted as their own links and referenced by id, mapped in `docs/case-studies/issue-468/formal-protocol-mapping.md` and pinned in `rust/tests/unit/agentic_coding.rs`. |
| R311 | The maintainer's position that everything is a link must be honored: the primitives are implemented as is, in the meta-language already in the code base. | Implemented: every primitive is emitted directly as a Links Notation record via `format_lino_record` (`rust/src/links_format.rs`) — there is no typed-struct or protocol-JSON layer — so each primitive *is* a link; mapped primitive by primitive in `docs/case-studies/issue-468/formal-protocol-mapping.md`. |
| R312 | A curated knowledge base for «Сказка о рыбаке и рыбке» must exercise all nine primitives end to end. | Implemented: formalizing the canonical synopsis yields **37 records** (1 header + 3 concepts + 4 entities + 6 predicates + 1 procedure + 2 contexts + 3 temporals + 3 modals + 7 annotations + 7 assertions); both the record count and `covers_all_nine()` are pinned in `rust/tests/unit/agentic_coding.rs`. |
| R313 | Deterministic extraction must be provided for the example, and general open-domain NL→KB extraction (which needs neural inference, a project NON-GOAL) must be scoped honestly rather than faked. | Implemented: every sentence becomes an `annotation` with real character offsets; the closed-class lexicon (`rust/src/agentic_coding/lexicon.rs`, data in `data/agentic-coding/fisherman-lexicon.lino`) turns recognised subject-predicate-object triples into structured assertions, and unrecognised sentences become honest natural-language assertions that never guess; general extraction is scoped as future work in `docs/case-studies/issue-468/README.md` §4.6/§7. |
| R314 | The title's "agentic mode" must be solved: the system must be driven by an agentic CLI against the OpenAI-compatible server — calling tools, understanding errors, web search/fetch, bash — while honoring the constraint not to wire external CLIs (claude/codex) into Formal AI. | **Implemented — the core task.** The deterministic planner `plan_chat_step` (`rust/src/agentic_coding/planner.rs`) drives the `web_search → web_fetch → write_file → run_command → final` loop, wired into the shared `agentic_outcome` decision (`rust/src/protocol.rs`) so all three OpenAI-shaped surfaces (`/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/messages`, `/v1/responses`) emit and consume tool calls identically; the in-repo `run_agentic_task` driver + offline corpus (`rust/src/agentic_coding/driver.rs`, `corpus.rs`) exercise it offline; gated by `agent_mode` + `pkg_agentic_coding`. External CLIs are documented as front-ends *against* the server in `docs/desktop/server-api.md`, never embedded. Pinned in `rust/tests/unit/agentic_coding.rs` and `rust/tests/unit/agentic_surfaces.rs`. |
| R315 | Issue-related data must be collected into `docs/case-studies/issue-468/`. | Implemented: `docs/case-studies/issue-468/raw-data/` holds `issue-468.json`, `issue-468-comments.json`, `pr-469.json`, `article-summary.md`, and `online-research.md`. |
| R316 | A deep case-study analysis must be produced, including online research for additional facts and data. | Implemented by `docs/case-studies/issue-468/README.md` §4 and `docs/case-studies/issue-468/raw-data/online-research.md` (8 cited sources: AMR, OpenIE, RDF reification/RDF-star, Wikidata qualifiers, FrameNet/PropBank, the NL→KB pipeline, the associative model, and the Tale provenance). |
| R317 | Each and all requirements from the issue must be listed. | Implemented: requirements R306–R319 enumerated here and in `docs/case-studies/issue-468/README.md` §3. |
| R318 | Possible solutions and solution plans must be proposed per requirement, checking existing components/libraries. | Implemented by `docs/case-studies/issue-468/README.md` §6 (per-requirement plans) and §7 (prior-art survey: `link-assistant/agent`/`opencode`/`codex`/`claude` as front-ends, the agentic-coding benchmarks already cataloged in `docs/benchmarks.md`, AMR, Stanford OpenIE, RDF reification/RDF-star/named graphs, Wikidata qualifiers, FrameNet/PropBank/VerbNet, `doublets-rs`, Neo4j). |
| R319 | Everything must be planned and executed in the single PR #469. | Implemented: the `rust/src/agentic_coding/` module, the `formal-ai agent` CLI subcommand, the two worked examples, the grounded recipe, the case study and protocol→links mapping, the `raw-data/` captures, these requirement rows, the changelog fragments, and `rust/tests/unit/agentic_coding.rs` + `rust/tests/unit/agentic_surfaces.rs` + `rust/tests/unit/specification/agentic_meta_algorithm.rs` all land in PR #469. |

## Issue #563 Repository Resource Summarization

Issue [#563](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/563) asks the
summarization pipeline to handle arbitrary repository files, formalize each file
before summarizing it, recurse into Markdown embedded grammars, and preserve the
issue research under `docs/case-studies/issue-563`. PR
[#564](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/564) adds a repository
file formalization boundary on top of the existing deterministic
`formalize -> summarize -> deformalize` pipeline. New rows R345-R354 capture the issue-specific obligations; each is implemented and covered by the tests its row names, with the documents covered by `rust/tests/unit/docs_requirements/issue_563.rs`.

Review feedback on PR #564 (konard) made the generalization explicit: the
solution must not stay file-specialized, but follow the meta algorithm —
describe the task, formalize it to the meta language, decompose, solve, and
compose — so that *any* repository resource can be summarized, **including
folders**, not only files. Rows R355-R359 capture this generalization, implemented and covered by `rust/tests/unit/specification/summarization_pipeline.rs` and the source-mirror tests each row names: a
directory is summarized by the recursive decompose -> summarize -> compose loop
(`rust/src/summarization/resource.rs`), with recursion depth bounded by the
summarization mode ladder.

JavaScript twin (PR #1188, 2026-10-08, JavaScript-first doctrine R997): `js/agentic/crate/summarization.mjs` (mirrors `mod.rs`), `summarization_markdown.mjs`, `summarization_dialog.mjs`, `summarization_file.mjs`, `summarization_resource.mjs`, `summarization_identifier.mjs` and `summarization_vocabulary.mjs` port the #563 surface, with every wording read from `data/meta/agentic-messages.lino` and the summary-cue meanings. `rust/tests/web/issue-0563-repository-summarization.test.mjs` replays the Rust tests named below on the same inputs and committed fixtures, plus conversation summaries captured from the prebuilt `formal-ai` 0.347.0 binary. Not yet at parity: the `meta_language` parse evidence of a code file, which the Rust build takes from the `meta-language` crate for 17 grammars; the JavaScript root carries it only for Rust (`summarization_meta_language.mjs` over the vendored tree-sitter-rust), no host installs that parser by default, and its four numbers are pinned by shape, not by a native run. `describe_project` and the #844/#893 layers (`importance`, `context`, `dedup`, `recheck`, `pipeline`, `gathering`, `validation`) have no JavaScript twin yet.

| ID | Requirement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R345 | The system must summarize arbitrary files from this repository, not only existing curated summarization inputs. | Implemented by `rust/src/summarization/file.rs::{formalize_repository_file,summarize_repository_file}` and public re-exports from `rust/src/lib.rs`; covered by `rust/tests/unit/specification/summarization_pipeline.rs::repository_file_summary_recurses_into_markdown_embedded_grammars`. JavaScript twin pinned by `rust/tests/web/issue-0563-repository-summarization.test.mjs` (`repository_file_summary_recurses_into_markdown_embedded_grammars`). |
| R346 | The implementation should start from two random repository files, summarize them manually, and generalize the algorithm beyond those exact files. | Implemented by `docs/case-studies/issue-563/raw-data/random-files-sampled.txt` and `manual-random-file-summaries.md`; the code handles generic code, structured data, Markdown, and fallback text rather than hardcoding the sampled JSON files. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/specification/summarization_pipeline.rs` (`the_sampled_repository_files_are_formalized_by_format_not_by_name`: both sampled JSON files are read as structured data by format, and an unknown format falls back to sentence statements) and `rust/tests/unit/docs_requirements/issue_563.rs`. JavaScript twin pinned by `rust/tests/web/issue-0563-repository-summarization.test.mjs` (`the_sampled_repository_files_are_formalized_by_format_not_by_name`). |

## Issue #674 Arbitrary Natural-Language Programs

Issue [#674](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/674) (E55) closes
the `ARCHITECTURE.md` §16 question carried since the E20 batch: procedures stated
as ordinary prose fell outside the trigger/response subset `rust/src/skill_compiler.rs`
recognizes, so `docs/USER-JOURNEYS.md` F2 could only be scaffolded. PR
[#815](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/815) adds
`rust/src/skill_procedure.rs`, a seeded step vocabulary, and the solver wiring that
compiles, executes, restates, and honestly refuses such procedures.

| ID | Requirement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R550 | Compile a freely phrased multi-step procedure that matches no existing compiler template into an ordered, typed, executable program. | Implemented: `compile_procedure_with_ledger` in `rust/src/skill_procedure.rs` calls the public intent formalizer, decomposes the impulse through shared `ordered_requirement_spans`, maps each source-grounded requirement onto a typed operation, and requires both a trigger lead and at least two recognized steps; covered by `arbitrary_four_step_procedure_compiles_executes_and_restates_its_steps` and `compiler_reuses_intent_formalization_and_records_every_ordered_requirement`. The tests live in `rust/tests/unit/specification/arbitrary_skill_compilation.rs`; the JavaScript compiler twin (`js/agentic/crate/skill_procedure.mjs`) is pinned on the same procedure in `rust/tests/web/agentic-recipes-b.test.mjs` (`an arbitrary four-step procedure compiles and restates its steps`, `the compiler records every ordered requirement under the solver impulse`). |
| R551 | Grow the step vocabulary as data rather than Rust parser match arms. | Implemented: Seed meanings live in `data/seed/meanings-skill-procedure.lino`; reviewed multilingual aliases live in the append-only `data/meta/procedure-capability-ledger.lino`. Both feed the same classifier. Learned aliases may target only an operation with existing typed host semantics, so classification grows without generated parser branches or silently invented side effects. The ledger aliases are exercised by `named_gap_proposes_human_gated_learning_and_an_approved_lesson_generalizes` in `rust/tests/unit/specification/arbitrary_skill_compilation.rs`; the JavaScript twin reads the same seed meanings and the same ledger file (`js/agentic/crate/skill_procedure.mjs`), pinned in `rust/tests/web/agentic-recipes-b.test.mjs`. |
| R552 | Compile the same procedure in English, Russian, Hindi, and Chinese to the same skill links. | Implemented: `CompiledProcedure::links_notation` and `link_records` project canonical slugs only, and the content-addressed id is derived from that slug-only program; covered by `same_procedure_in_every_supported_language_compiles_to_the_same_skill_links`. The test lives in `rust/tests/unit/specification/arbitrary_skill_compilation.rs`; the JavaScript twin compiles the four languages to the same links in `rust/tests/web/agentic-recipes-b.test.mjs` (`the same procedure in every supported language compiles to the same skill links`). |
| R553 | Fail honestly with a named gap on an uncompilable step, record a `skill_gap` event, and compile nothing partially. | Implemented: `ProcedureCompileError::UncompilableStep` carries the clause, its span, and `no compiled capability for "…"`; `rust/src/solver_handlers/procedure_rules.rs` records both the gap and complete review-only proposal artifact, and emits no compiled prefix. Covered by `uncompilable_step_reports_a_named_gap_and_compiles_nothing_partially`, `solver_answers_an_uncompilable_step_with_the_gap_and_a_skill_gap_event`, and `solver_records_a_learning_proposal_but_still_compiles_nothing_on_a_gap`. The tests live in `rust/tests/unit/specification/arbitrary_skill_compilation.rs`; the JavaScript compiler twin reports the same named gap and compiles nothing in `rust/tests/web/agentic-recipes-b.test.mjs` (`an uncompilable step reports a named gap and compiles nothing`, `the gap name collapses the seed quote escape`). |
| R554 | Keep compiled skills inspectable: *"why did you do that?"* cites the compiled steps and their source sentence spans. | Implemented: Requirements and steps retain exact source text and UTF-8 byte spans. The solver persists the complete artifact in its assistant reply; `meta_explanation` parses and integrity-checks that artifact instead of recompiling a prior user turn. Covered by `solver_compiles_a_freely_phrased_procedure_and_can_restate_it_later` and `compiled_artifact_round_trips_executes_and_explains_without_recompiling_user_prose`. The tests live in `rust/tests/unit/specification/arbitrary_skill_compilation.rs`. |
| R555 | Persist a complete program that can be parsed and executed independently of the original compiler call. | Implemented: `artifact_links_notation` serializes the formalized impulse, requirements, provenance, canonical program, trigger, and steps; `from_artifact_links_notation` recomputes ids/program and validates spans before `ProcedureHost` walks it. The round-trip test also rejects a tampered content id. Pinned by `compiled_artifact_round_trips_executes_and_explains_without_recompiling_user_prose` in `rust/tests/unit/specification/arbitrary_skill_compilation.rs` and, for the JavaScript artifact twin (`js/agentic/crate/skill_procedure_artifact.mjs`), by `rust/tests/web/agentic-recipes-b.test.mjs` (`the compiled artifact round-trips and rejects tampering`). |
| R556 | Feed named gaps into automatic learning without letting automatic learning authorize behavior. | Implemented: Each gap deterministically creates a `ProcedureLearningProposal`. Given observed unsupported surfaces plus successful seeded paraphrases, `infer_candidate` derives the canonical typed operation itself and rejects conflicting meanings. `ProcedureCapabilityLedger::promote_candidate` then requires en/ru/hi/zh parity, a green named regression suite, and explicit non-empty human approval while preserving the inference evidence and content-addressed candidate id. Failure, tamper, promotion, and restart paths are covered by `named_gap_proposes_human_gated_learning_and_an_approved_lesson_generalizes`. The test lives in `rust/tests/unit/specification/arbitrary_skill_compilation.rs`. |
| R557 | Execute the same task through Formal AI's Agent path and preserve exact evidence. | Implemented: `rust/src/agentic_coding/procedure.rs` routes the shared compiled artifact through write, read-back verification, `formal-ai procedure conformance`, execution-result verification, and final response. `agentic_planner_writes_verifies_and_returns_the_same_compiled_artifact` and `public_cli_executes_the_persisted_artifact_with_the_same_interpreter` check the in-repo/public paths; `experiments/issue-674-agent-cli/run.sh` drives the external Agent CLI, byte-compares the artifact, and requires the conformance command in its preserved stream. The tests live in `rust/tests/unit/specification/arbitrary_skill_compilation.rs`; the JavaScript Agent path (`js/agentic/procedure.mjs`) writes, verifies, executes and returns the same artifact in `rust/tests/web/agentic-recipes-b.test.mjs` (`Agent CLI procedure: write, verify, execute, and return the same artifact`, `Agent CLI procedure rejects a corrupted readback and a failed execution`). |
| R558 | Verify the ambitious requirement set both leaf-by-leaf and as one task. | Implemented: `cargo test --test unit arbitrary_skill_compilation` contains focused decomposition, canonicalization, failure, artifact, learning, and Agent tests plus `whole_task_uses_one_artifact_across_solver_interpreter_explanation_and_agent`, which carries one artifact across the solver, parser/interpreter, later explanation, and Agent planner. The suite is `rust/tests/unit/specification/arbitrary_skill_compilation.rs`. |

## Issue #708 Bounded Natural-Language Memory Programs

Issue [#708](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/708) (E66)
requires associative-memory requests to compile into one inspectable,
permissioned Links Notation program rather than disappear into handler control
flow. PR [#883](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/883) adds a
closed seeded algebra, explicit caller-derived bounds, editable review shapes,
and matching native/browser interpreters.

| ID | Requirement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R708-1 | Natural-language memory requests must compile into an executable program using only the closed primitive set `match`, `create`, `update`, `delete_with_retraction`, `map_matches`, `filter`, `sequential_compose`, and bounded fixpoint iteration. | `rust/src/memory_program.rs` compiles only complete families from `data/seed/memory-programs.lino`; `rust/src/memory_program/execution.rs` interprets the closed enum. Covered by `fifteen_seeded_query_families_compile_with_a_program_trace` and the parser unit suite. |
| R708-2 | Equivalent English, Russian, Hindi, and Chinese requests must produce the same program; the current language protocol additionally requires Spanish. | Language is excluded from canonical identity while bindings, limits, permissions, and steps remain included. Covered by `equivalent_multilingual_requests_compile_to_the_same_program_links`, the browser multilingual case, and language-parity checks. |
| R708-3 | Compilation and execution must remain inspectable: show program, stable id, permissions, limits, matched ids, outcome, halt reason, and an honest `program_gap`. | The shared query surface embeds the serialized program and execution trace; unmatched memory cues report `program_gap` without partial compilation. Covered by `query_surface_traces_the_compiled_program_and_names_program_gaps`. |
| R708-4 | Bounds must come from task decomposition depth, stop before unsafe partial effects, and distinguish fixpoint from a bound stop. | `MemoryProgramLimits::from_decomposition_depth` derives iteration and match caps, serializes them into program identity, and the interpreter reports `match_limit` or `iteration_limit`. Covered by `bounds_stop_honestly_before_partial_writes`. |
| R708-5 | Destructive effects require explicit confirmation and preserve append-only history. | Permission is seed-owned and revalidated after edits; `delete_with_retraction` is refused without `DestructiveConfirmed` and appends a retraction rather than erasing its target. Covered by `destructive_program_requires_confirmation_and_appends_a_retraction`. |
| R708-6 | Reviewers must be able to parse, edit, and re-execute the visible `replace x y` and `when n do m` forms without a hidden permission escalation. | The parser makes the visible forms authoritative, rebuilds affected steps, reapplies seed permissions, and recomputes canonical identity. Covered by `compiled_program_round_trips_replace_and_when_do_shapes`. |
| R708-7 | At least 15 families must include selective contributed-fact rename, weekly topic summary, and missing-Russian-label todos. | The seed contains exactly 15 reviewed families across reads, writes, mapping, filtering, retraction, and fixpoint normalization. Covered by the 15-family compiler regression and the native execution suite. |
| R708-8 | Mapping must affect execution, and the same compile/execute/persist/refuse/gap semantics must work in native and browser memory. | Both interpreters carry `map_matches` state into aggregation and source-preserving collection copies; browser events are atomically persisted to IndexedDB. Covered by `mapped_copy_retains_source_content_and_collection` and `rust/tests/e2e/tests/issue-708.spec.js`. |
| R708-9 | The solution must document the link-cli operation census, natural-language triple-store querying, bounded Datalog relationship, and self-application evidence. | Implemented: `docs/case-studies/issue-708/README.md` records the source-pinned census and conservative boundedness decision; `issue_708_self_hosting` byte-checks three Agent-CLI-authored leaves, satisfying the repository's 20% self-hosting gate. |

## Issue #710 Dynamic Coding Discovery Continuation

The 2026-09-14 continuation audited every coding and benchmark requirement,
removed benchmark-specific synthesis bodies, and connected structural task
recognition to licensed external parts, composition, bounded verification, and
rediscoverable procedure memory. The implementation plan and before-state
evidence live in `docs/case-studies/issue-710/plans/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R710-D1 | Coding synthesis must derive answers from task structure and sourced operations, never from upstream case names or copied task sentences. | Implemented by `task_spec`, `concept_discovery`, and `composition`; `coding_discovery::no_memorization` scans the downloaded HumanEval/MBPP slice against `rust/src/` and `data/seed/`. |
| R710-D2 | The full HumanEval suite (164 cases) must be run honestly through the discovery path and report its upstream grading result, with the first-20 slice retained as a regression control. | Implemented by `benchmark run --suite humaneval --slice 164`, cold-offline and with `--online`; the committed 2026-09-17 full-slice row passes 14/164 upstream tests with `--online` (a cold-offline run in the same session scored 9/164), and the 2026-09-15 first-20 row — 20/20, with an empty-source-cache control — stays as the regression control. |
| R710-D3 | The full MBPP suite (500 cases) must be run honestly through the same discovery path and upstream assertions, with the first-20 slice retained as a regression control. | Implemented by `benchmark run --suite mbpp --slice 500`, cold-offline and with `--online`; the committed 2026-09-18 full-slice rows pass 49/500 cold-offline and 60/500 with `--online`, and the 2026-09-15 first-20 row — 20/20 `--online`, with a cold offline control at 18/20 naming the two externally defined sequence gaps — stays as the regression control. |
| R710-D4 | Structural coding prompts must enter program synthesis before arithmetic or concept lookup. | Implemented by `coding::task_spec::recognise` in intent formalization and handler precedence; pinned by `coding_discovery::routing`. |
| R710-D5 | Upstream benchmark runs must have an explicit online-discovery mode while PR ratchet checks remain offline. | Implemented by `benchmark run --online`, `run_suite_with_online`, and the scheduled workflow contract; pinned by `specification::external_benchmarks`. |
| R710-D6 | Wikifunctions, Python standard-library documentation, and Rosetta Code must be consumable as licensed, content-addressed function/example sources. | Implemented under `rust/src/coding/function_catalog/` with captured fixtures and `coding_discovery::{wikifunctions,python_docs,rosetta}`. |
| R710-D7 | The coding research contract must name the real external source formats accepted by discovery, while the older procedure-rewrite loop remains explicit. | Implemented in `data/meta/coding-research-learning-contract.lino`; source-specific offline replay is pinned by the coding-discovery source tests. |
| R710-D8 | Requirement sentences must become a language-neutral concept map of structural meanings, candidate parts, evidence, and blocked needs. | Implemented by `concept_discovery::discover`; pinned by `coding_discovery::concepts`. |
| R710-D9 | Candidate parts must be composed into multiple drafts and selected only after CST validation and bounded executable tests. | Implemented by `composition::compose`, `python_render`, and `AgentWorkspace`; pinned by `coding_discovery::composition`. |
| R710-D10 | A verified coding procedure must be content-addressed, provenance-bearing, tamper-detecting, forgettable, and rediscoverable. | Implemented by `DiscoveredProcedureLedger`; pinned by `coding_discovery::ledger`. |
| R710-D11 | Conversational discovery must preserve the same task and concept identities across English, Russian, Hindi, Chinese, and Spanish. | Implemented with seed roles and structural meanings; pinned by the 25 held-out cases in `coding_discovery::multilingual`. |
| R710-D12 | “Count to N inclusive” must derive a complete parameterized range rather than resolve a fixed catalog task. | Implemented by the `range_inclusive` composition with a literal or parameter bound; pinned for N=100 in five languages. This is the coding-discovery portion of #1071, not the whole issue. |
| R710-D13 | Rosetta Code example requests must return attributed, non-generated code; execute-URL requests must run Rust only in the bounded workspace and must never become shell copy commands. | Implemented by `rosetta_code::fetch_example` and `try_rosetta_code_request`; pinned by the exact #862/#863 prompts and four-language paraphrases. |
| R710-D14 | A dated upstream result may regress only against the floor in force at that date; pull requests still may not lower any recorded result or floor. | Implemented by `external_benchmarks::ratchet`; pinned by the historical-floor regression tests. |
| R710-D15 | Published current benchmark numbers must be derived from the latest committed ledger rows, with newer local measurements clearly separated. | Implemented: `docs/benchmarks.md` publishes the per-suite table pinned cell-for-cell to the latest committed rows of `data/benchmarks/external-results.lino`, `VISION.md` must contain every suite's latest passed/total and run date, and `ROADMAP.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, and `README.md` must carry the latest committed HumanEval and MBPP rows; pinned by `docs_benchmarks::latest_external_rows_are_published_from_the_ledger`, with upstream-beside-curated co-presence across the same documents pinned by `docs_benchmarks::curated_pass_ratios_publish_an_upstream_comparison_beside_them`. |
| R710-D16 | This batch must carry a Formal-AI-authored leaf with model, session, evidence, and pull-request attribution. | Delivered by the self-hosting authoring run recorded in the commit trailers; automated by `specification::self_hosting_metric`. Manual confirmation is not yet recorded. |

## Issue #710 Repository Completion and Durable Retention Continuation

The 2026-09-15 maintainer continuation requires complete issue-driven repository
tasks, recursive trusted-source discovery and safe forgetting. Earlier green
benchmark slices do not establish these broader capabilities. Plan 06 in
`docs/case-studies/issue-710/plans/` is the active resumable audit.

| ID | Requirement | Status / evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R710-R1 | Bind implementation language, source destination and output operands independently; preserve ordered output clauses. | Literal stdout composition in Rust, Kotlin, Scala and Python; `process_composition` and `issue_1133_hive_mind_three_runs` test renamed paths and filename-shaped output. Arbitrary program behavior remains open. |
| R710-R2 | Include requested CI, runtime setup, comments, run instructions and executable output assertions. | Source-backed primitive records and shared recipe workflow generation; verifier mutation tests reject wrong case, extra LF and nonzero exit. Live Python project passes. Kotlin local execution still stops at a missing compiler. |
| R710-R3 | Discover missing runtime prerequisites recursively and recover from observed failures. | Partial: recipe replay resumes after a bound successful retry and retains the original failure. Discovery is now in place through issue #1138 B6 (`docs/requirements/issue-1138-prerequisite-discovery.md`): a missing executable becomes a blocked prerequisite need distinguished from permission denial and compile errors (`rust/tests/unit/issue_1138_prerequisite_need.rs`), setup steps come only from the trusted publisher and recurse over dependencies with cycles named and shared setups installed once (`rust/tests/unit/issue_1138_setup_publisher.rs`), and installation is consent-gated and workspace-scoped (`rust/tests/unit/issue_1138_install_scope.rs`). Still open, re-checked 2026-10-08: no run has yet recovered on its own — the held-out `zig` and `gleam` self-use observations (`rust/tests/unit/issue_1138_self_use_toolchain.rs`) ran with the default refused install grant, so nothing was installed and no task finished after a missing compiler; generating a workflow does not prove local compiler recovery. |
| R710-R4 | A successful tool result must be bound to the requested path, bytes and ordered command before it counts as execution evidence. | Implemented: `recipe_evidence` and `issue_908` retain actual assistant calls and reject orphan, duplicate, unrelated and out-of-order results, including during recovery. Unrelated setup cannot clear a failed step. The same binding applies outside the recipe path: `ObligationLedger::observe` returns `None` for a record whose command or path answers no expectation, so an unrelated result cannot clear any obligation on any surface. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/recipe_evidence.rs`, `rust/tests/unit/issue_908.rs`. |
| R710-R5 | Commit only the recipe's artifacts, excluding compiler outputs and unrelated staged files. | Implemented: Explicit-path staging and `git commit --only`; `issue_1133_hive_mind_three_runs` preserves branch/commit evidence assertions. Explicit requests to commit uncommitted repository changes keep their separate semantics. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1133_hive_mind_three_runs.rs`. |
| R710-R6 | Preserve original dialogue and observations, unknown legacy records, and imported custom knowledge unless the user authorizes deletion/modification. | Implemented: Provenance-first classification, apply-time revalidation and duplicate-ID safety; `memory_retention_origin`, `memory_learning`, existing deletion/reset and export/import tests. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/memory_retention_origin.rs`, `rust/tests/unit/memory_learning.rs`. |
| R710-R7 | Forget only reconstructable cache data; keep the rediscovery recipe and provenance, accounting for retained metadata. | Reconstruction records survive restart and further pressure in `memory_retention_origin`; a public URL authorizes reacquisition, not replacement of historical evidence with today's content. End-to-end automatic source-cache reconstruction remains open. |
| R710-R8 | Formal AI must perform meaningful work through Agent CLI, and failures must become general regression cases. | Live Python project and grounded source-identifier rename succeed. The open-ended refactor only read its input; executable authoring-helper regressions now reject unchanged seed/destination bytes before publishing. Kotlin recovery, semantic formalization and open-ended regression authorship remain open. Re-checked 2026-10-08: every PR #1188 dogfood failure became a pinned regression (docs/case-studies/pull-request-1188/formal-ai-dogfood.md, T1 to T22), and after being taught Formal AI wrote ledger rows T21 and T22 itself. |
| R710-R9 | Retain every requirement as a verifiable obligation; unknown clauses cannot be silently discarded. | Implemented: Shared decomposition preserves operands, addresses, list clauses and byte provenance (`requirement_span_integrity`); inline formalization preserves source identity (`issue_956`). The need ledger distinguishes selected methods from satisfied results, preventing pre-execution success and skill claims. Preserving unknown text still does not interpret it, but it is no longer discarded: an unrecognized clause becomes an `Underivable` obligation node that is split and, failing that, reported as a named gap with its byte span. Obligation-ledger execution and runtime verification feedback are delivered by `rust/src/obligation_ledger.rs`. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/requirement_span_integrity.rs`, `rust/tests/unit/issue_956.rs`, `rust/tests/unit/specification/obligation_ledger.rs`. |
| R710-R10 | Report proven wrapper/client defects upstream without publishing private traces. | Withdrawn from this repository: Hive Mind #2259 contains the reviewed MCP transport reproduction; no current Agent CLI defect has been established from the compiler failures. The reproduction lives upstream in Hive Mind #2259; nothing in formal-ai is left to change. |

## Issue #847 Task Decomposition As A Working Task

Issue [#847](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/847) (E57)
records that both halves of decomposition were refused: "split this task into
subtasks" and "is this task atomic?" fell through to the unknown-prompt
fallback or misrouted to `write_program`. PR
[#857](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/857) makes decomposition
a working task — one recursion seen from two sides, recognised from seed
surfaces rather than per-language phrase lists (issue #386), with the atomicity
judgement as its base case.

| ID | Requirement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R847-1 | Decomposition must be a recognised intent in every supported language, never the unknown-prompt fallback, with the surfaces in seed data and no per-language phrase list in Rust. | `data/seed/meanings-decomposition.lino` carries the splitting, sub-task, atomicity, first-step and enumeration roles for en/ru/hi/zh; `rust/src/solver_handlers/task_decomposition.rs::classify` names only the roles. Covered by `splitting_is_recognised_in_every_supported_language` and `decomposition_is_recognised_in_every_supported_language`. |
| R847-2 | Splitting a task must yield children that each carry an observable completion criterion. | `is_checkable` in `rust/src/task_decomposition.rs` rejects unobservable fragments such as "understand the codebase" and merges them into a sibling; covered by `every_child_has_an_observable_completion_criterion` and `an_unobservable_fragment_never_becomes_a_child`. |
| R847-3 | "Is this task atomic?" must be answerable standalone and must be the recursion's base case. | `DecompositionQuestion::Atomicity` answers from the same `decompose_task` call the split answer uses, so the two cannot disagree; covered by `atomicity_is_recognised_in_every_supported_language` and `asking_whether_a_task_is_atomic_is_answered_standalone`. |
| R847-4 | The recursion must terminate: every leaf atomic, or `max_decomposition_depth` reached and reported rather than hidden. | `decompose_task` records an `AtomicityReason` per leaf and `Decomposition::depth_bound_reached` drives the reported note and the per-row markers from one test; covered by `recursion_terminates_with_atomic_leaves_or_a_reported_depth_bound` and `the_configured_depth_bound_is_reported_in_the_answer`. |
| R847-5 | Every sub-task must be a first-class inspectable `sub_impulse:` event, reusing the existing structure. | `record_task_decomposition` appends one `sub_impulse` event per sub-task, so each surfaces as a `sub_impulse:<id>` evidence link; covered by `every_sub_task_surfaces_as_a_sub_impulse_event` and `every_sub_task_is_an_inspectable_sub_impulse_event`. |
| R847-6 | The decomposition must be deterministic: the same task and configuration always produce the same result. | The splitter is a pure function of the task text and the depth bound, with no clock, randomness or ordering by hash; covered by `decomposition_is_deterministic_for_a_given_config` and `decomposition_is_deterministic`. |
| R847-7 | A real corpus task must decompose into children a human agrees are smaller and jointly sufficient. | Covered by `a_real_corpus_task_splits_into_smaller_jointly_sufficient_children`, which splits this repository's own `experiments/` code-change-detector task into its two edits. |
| R847-8 | The spectrum must run from a GitHub issue down to a single atomic edit, with regression coverage in the specification suites in all four languages. | Implemented: `the_spectrum_runs_from_issue_to_atomic_edit` pins both ends of the ladder; `rust/tests/unit/specification/task_decomposition.rs` holds the four-language specifications and `rust/tests/unit/issue_847_task_decomposition.rs` the reproduction cases. |

## Issue #848 Executable Coding Tasks

Issue [#848](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/848) asks for
an honest, broad measurement of Formal AI doing real coding work through the
Agent CLI. The v0.303.0 baseline passed 38/130 tasks; the prepared branch
passed 45/130 with no test authoring or targeted edit. PR
[#897](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/897) adds a semantic,
observed execution floor and makes the ladder reject false greens. See
`docs/case-studies/issue-848/` for the full evidence and residual boundary. The
final complete v0.320.0 measurement passes 65/130 tasks (L2 5/12, L3 10/28).

| ID | Requirement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R848-1 | A complete run must measure all 130 tasks and never confuse a filtered diagnostic or unavailable server with the canonical score. | Implemented: The runner records completeness and `not_measured`, writes filtered results separately, persists every task incrementally, and requires absence of the launcher success marker before diagnostic text can mean the server never started. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_848_coding_ladder.rs` (`compiler_measurement_and_same_task_authorship_are_preserved` holds the runner to `dataset_total`, `complete`, the separate partial results and the `not_measured` launcher check). |
| R848-2 | Source creation must render executable bytes from the formalized request, never echo request prose, and must observe the exact target after writing. | Implemented: `rust/src/agentic_coding/code_task.rs` lowers seed-backed function, constant, and test concepts and verifies with an exact `cat`. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_848_coding_ladder.rs` (`rust_function_request_writes_executable_source_and_observes_it`, `rust_constant_request_writes_source_and_observes_it`, `rust_test_request_writes_source_and_observes_it`, `rust_addition_test_preserves_the_requested_expression`); the agentic planner twin writes and observes the same bytes in `rust/tests/web/issue-0848-coding-ladder.test.mjs`. |
| R848-3 | New Rust targets must compile before the ladder credits them. | Implemented: The real-client harness invokes `rustc` only for requested targets that did not exist before the task. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_848_coding_ladder.rs` (`compiler_measurement_and_same_task_authorship_are_preserved` holds the `rustc --edition=2024` call to the targets that did not exist before the task). |
| R848-4 | The full result must have nonzero `test_authoring`, `targeted_edit`, L2, and L3 outcomes. | Implemented: The complete ladder result records all four above zero; deterministic regressions pin source generation and grounded edits. The v0.320.0 measurement (65/130, L2 5/12, L3 10/28) is held in the case study by `rust/tests/unit/issue_848_coding_ladder.rs` (`case_study_and_release_trace_every_issue_848_acceptance_boundary`), and the capabilities behind the test-authoring and targeted-edit outcomes by the deterministic regressions in the same file. |
| R848-5 | Repository search must use the named code subject rather than the full conversational prompt. | Implemented: `rust/src/agentic_coding/shell_command.rs` emits one focused query; seven independent subject shapes are covered. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_848_coding_ladder.rs` (`repository_searches_use_the_named_code_subject`) and, on the agentic planner twin, by `rust/tests/web/issue-0848-coding-ladder.test.mjs`. |
| R848-6 | Structured collection edits must transform existing workspace bytes and verify the written result. | Implemented: `rust/src/agentic_coding/structured_edit.rs` implements read → transform → write → exact observation. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_848_coding_ladder.rs` (`collection_edit_reads_transforms_writes_and_observes_workspace_bytes`) and, on the agentic planner twin, by `rust/tests/web/issue-0848-coding-ladder.test.mjs`. |
| R848-7 | The approach must work across supported languages and benchmark facts must track the repository version. | Implemented: Coding meanings cover en/ru/hi/zh; file-derived expectations resolve the current version from `Cargo.toml` and fail closed. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_848_coding_ladder.rs` (`multilingual_rust_function_requests_generate_source`, `coding_source_templates_and_outcomes_are_seed_grounded`, and the runner checks of `compiler_measurement_and_same_task_authorship_are_preserved`); the Russian, Chinese and Hindi requests generate the same source on the JavaScript root in `rust/tests/web/issue-0848-coding-ladder.test.mjs`. |
| R848-8 | At least 20% of reviewed smallest leaves must be completed through Formal AI and the real Agent CLI. | Implemented: Sessions `ses_04160c59fffe3FDUKteR56kfQp`, `ses_03d2e0597ffeAUZhq3qAtj2I4U`, `ses_03d2df24effeijLfzPXiUeV4pG`, and `ses_03d2ddb1cffeQkS5gxWjpMojc6` authored four of seven leaves (57%); exact client/server logs, canonical artifacts, and replays are committed. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_848_coding_ladder.rs` (`isolated_solve_stdout_is_explicitly_transported_into_the_benchmark_tree` holds the decomposition, the sessions and the authored artifact). |
| R848-9 | Repeated verified workspace changes may become reusable procedures only after a review-gated learning cycle, and unapproved candidates must remain inert. | Implemented: `rust/src/workspace_change_learning.rs` separates task and execution fingerprints, records exact successful observations, forms candidates after two distinct tasks, requires a named approval and zero-failure gate, and exposes execution only for content-addressed approved-ledger recipes. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_848_workspace_change_learning.rs` (`exact_observations_infer_a_candidate_but_cannot_activate_it`, `only_a_green_named_review_promotes_and_replays_the_held_out_rewrite`, `formal_ai_authored_contract_policy_and_fixture_are_runtime_evidence`). |
| R848-10 | Symbol refactors and composite module requests must transform grounded workspace bytes, verify each effect exactly, and terminate. | Implemented: `rust/src/agentic_coding/workspace_change.rs` uses the shared bounded Normal Markov executor, a compact edit or validated repeated-identifier command, and exact SHA-256 observations; composite requests perform an observed source write followed by a compact registration edit. Issue #848 regressions cover Agent absolute paths, repeated matches, write-only fallback, and both transaction effects. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_848_coding_ladder.rs` (`identifier_refactor_is_a_grounded_verified_rewrite_not_a_file_move`, `identifier_refactor_accepts_agent_cli_absolute_tool_paths`, `composite_module_request_creates_source_and_registers_the_module`, `composite_module_uses_a_compact_agent_registration_edit`) and, on the agentic planner twin, by `rust/tests/web/issue-0848-coding-ladder.test.mjs`. |

## Issue #890 Formal Proof Program Translation

Issue [#890](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/890) closes the
gap between solving a formal constraint and presenting its proof in an
executable programming language. The proof is a semantic value first; prose and
program syntax are projections of that value.

| ID | Requirement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R890-1 | A formal proof must be represented independently from natural-language prose and programming-language syntax. | Implemented: `FormalProof::IntegerInterval` stores bounds, inclusivity, satisfiability, and a witness; `proof_meaning_is_independent_from_its_programming_language_presentations` verifies canonical statement round trips and renderer independence. |
| R890-2 | The same solved proof must translate to at least two programming languages through the general code meta-language path. | Implemented: `CodeMeaning::FormalProof` formalizes once and `render_code_meaning` projects through `data/seed/proof-program-templates.lino` to Rust or Python without a direct source-target pair; `same_solved_proof_uses_general_translation_path_for_two_targets` checks both targets share one `meaning:` link. |
| R890-3 | Generated proof programs must compile or execute where the environment supports it. | Implemented: `generated_proof_programs_compile_and_execute` compiles the Rust renderer with `rustc`, executes it, runs the Python renderer with `python3`, and requires both witnesses to print `2`. |
| R890-4 | Every registered supported natural language must be able to request proof translation. | Implemented: `every_registered_natural_language_can_request_proof_translation` covers and compares the live `supported_languages()` registry: English, Russian, Hindi, and Chinese. |
| R890-5 | The native and browser surfaces must expose the same proof-translation behavior, with a whole-task regression. | Implemented: `whole_issue_890_workflow_solves_translates_and_executes` covers the native composition; `rust/tests/e2e/tests/issue-890.spec.js` covers Rust and Python plus all registered natural-language request forms in the browser worker. |
| R890-6 | Issue, PR, related-work, online-research, requirement, plan, and release evidence must remain traceable in the repository. | Implemented: `issue_890_case_study_and_release_metadata_are_traceable` guards `docs/case-studies/issue-890`, this matrix, architecture, roadmap, and the minor changelog fragment. |
| R890-7 | At least one of the five reviewed implementation leaves must be authored through the real Formal AI/Agent CLI loop and reproducible byte-for-byte. | Implemented: Session `ses_03b44e557ffeSQeAuCYzxfc3BR` authored the proof invariant leaf, captured under `docs/case-studies/issue-890/agent-cli-evidence`; `agent_cli_authorship_leaf_is_byte_exact_and_reproducible` guards the artifact, session, raw stream, and replay script. |

Issue [#919](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/919) closes the
procedure-learning gap between named program synthesis failures and the
existing cached research and bounded workspace execution machinery. Detailed
design, alternatives, standards research, and verification live in
`docs/case-studies/issue-919/`.

| --- | --- | --- |
| R919-1 | A real coding synthesis miss must enter the loop as its recorded stable skill-gap identity. | Delivered: `rust/tests/unit/issue_919.rs` starts with the real unsupported Ruby `count_to_three` request, asserts `write_program_skill_gap`, and carries the matching `program_skill_gap` identity into `CodingResearchGap`. |
| R919-2 | Research must be query-planned, provenance-bearing, cacheable, and formalized into the meta-language before compilation. | Delivered: The original `coding_research_learning::research_coding_skill_gap` loop accepts the repository's licensed `formal_ai_coding_procedure_v1` rewrite format. Since the 2026-09-15 #710 continuation, sibling discovery adapters also formalize Python documentation HTML, Wikifunctions Z8/Z14/Z20 JSON, and Rosetta MediaWiki wikitext into content-addressed parts. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_919.rs`::`coding_gap_is_solved_by_a_verified_researched_procedure_and_replays_offline`. |
| R919-3 | A researched procedure must be marked and pass the same bounded execution verification as a hand-seeded procedure before it is kept. | Delivered: `origin research` rewrite candidates still use #897's `execute_workspace_rewrite`; dynamically composed Python and Rosetta Rust candidates use `AgentWorkspace`. Only verified results enter their respective procedure ledgers. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_919.rs` (`coding_gap_is_solved_by_a_verified_researched_procedure_and_replays_offline`, `failed_execution_is_not_kept_and_schedules_the_next_research_round`). |
| R919-4 | Full provenance and deterministic offline replay must survive CI. | Delivered: The ledger retains query, URL, declared SPDX license, fetch time, source hash, formalization, executor, output hash, step count, and reviewer. The regression proves a default-offline client makes no transport calls and reproduces the proposal, id, ledger, and output from cache. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_919.rs`::`coding_gap_is_solved_by_a_verified_researched_procedure_and_replays_offline`. |
| R919-5 | Failed rounds must remain non-executable and update the gap to drive the next research round. | Delivered: A mismatched execution rejects the candidate, leaves the ledger empty, appends query/reason to the gap, and schedules `alternative evidence round 2`. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_919.rs`::`failed_execution_is_not_kept_and_schedules_the_next_research_round`. |
| R919-6 | The loop must follow a data-authored contract and build on the completed E69 dependency. | Delivered: `data/meta/coding-research-learning-contract.lino` pins the source, provenance, execution, live/offline, review, and recovery boundaries; E69 issue #916 / PR #966 is merged. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_919.rs`::`coding_research_policy_is_data_authored_and_pins_the_safety_boundaries`. |

# Issue #936 Substitution-Rule Compilation

Issue [#936](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/936) is E84:
compile the existing Turing-complete substitution-rule representation to
embeddable targets while retaining Rust ownership and the verified synthesis
path. The implementation and evidence are described in
[`../case-studies/issue-936/`](../../case-studies/issue-936/README.md).

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R936-1 | Lower `replace x y`, `when n do m`, variables, and ordered composition through one target-neutral compiler IR. | Delivered: `rust/src/substitution_compiler/mod.rs` defines the serializable IR and lowers every parsed condition/action/pattern; `counter_loop_executes_identically_in_rust_javascript_and_webassembly` exercises conditions, multiple actions, shared bindings, and three composed rewrites. |
| R936-2 | Make generated Rust the canonical executable target. | Delivered: `rust.rs` and `rust_runtime.rs` emit a standalone stdin/stdout program whose bounded fixpoint and ordered graph semantics match `SubstitutionGraph`; the parity test compiles it with `rustc -D warnings`. |
| R936-3 | Provide JavaScript and WebAssembly for embedding without growing parallel JavaScript logic. | Delivered: Both targets execute the generated Rust runtime as WASM. The JavaScript primary is an ES-module interoperability bridge with no matching/rewrite implementation; the test rejects an `applyRule` mirror and executes both targets through Node. |
| R936-4 | Export only a proven synthesized program plan. | Delivered: `ProgramPlan::compile` rejects unchanged or guard-terminated plans. `try_export_substitution_program` reuses `construct_rule_from_unknown` and its semantic fixture before compiling; `program_plan_exports_only_after_a_verified_finite_rewrite` pins the gate. |
| R936-5 | Let users request any target through the existing solver in English, Russian, Hindi, and Chinese. | Delivered: Target/export cues and localized responses live in seed data; `verified_program_plan_exports_are_seeded_in_all_supported_languages` asserts routing, verification evidence, named source, target, and executable recipe for all four languages and all targets. |
| R936-6 | Verify a small loop/counter against the interpreter on every target and export and execute a prompt result. | Delivered: The cross-target test performs exact output comparison; the example records a native Rust run in `manual-export-run.log`. `run_issue_936.sh` additionally resumes a real Agent CLI session, writes JavaScript/WASM/IR/input artifacts, compiles them, and pins the exact Node output in `agent-cli-export-e2e/`. |
| R936-7 | Preserve root cause, red/green tests, self-development attempts, release metadata, one-PR traceability, and at least one genuinely self-authored leaf. | Delivered: Session `ses_ff77c472cffej9Hmz346niSMgQ` authored `data/meta/substitution-compiler-contract.lino`; its byte-identical artifact and raw traces are under `self-hosting-authorship/`. The case study, this matrix, E84 roadmap/architecture entries, changelog fragment, and PR [#1016](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/1016) form the review record. |

## Issue #1021 Full-Range Coding And Contribution Artifacts

Issue [#1021](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1021) collects
the prompts Formal AI answered wrongly, the capabilities a contribution needs to
land, and the demand that the whole loop be test-covered in one pull request.
See PR #1027 and `docs/case-studies/issue-1021/`.

The rule the issue states first governs every row below: "solve by
generalization, not specialization -- a per-prompt fix that makes one task pass
is a regression against that instruction, not progress". Rows marked **not
delivered** are reported rather than quietly narrowed, per the issue's own "the
bar is not to be met by lowering it".

| R1021-34 | A gate that reports a failure names the thing that failed, not the healthy things beside it. | Implemented: The `Broken Link Checker` failed three times over links that answer 200, because `extractBrokenUrls` in `scripts/check-web-archive.mjs` located the failing part of lychee's report by searching for one hard-coded `## Errors per input` heading. lychee writes only the sections a run has links for, so a report whose sole failure was a timeout matched nothing and fell back to parsing the whole document, harvesting every healthy redirect in it. Sections are now sliced out by heading and a section counts as failing unless its category is one of the outcomes known to be healthy -- selection by exclusion, so an unrecognised future category is reported rather than silently dropped, because a false positive is loud and a dropped failure is not. The four tests added to `scripts/check-web-archive.test.mjs` cover the shapes the old lookup got wrong (`reports a timeout when the report has no errors section`, `collects failures from every failing section, not just the first`, `treats an unrecognised section as failing`, `ignores the summary table and the healthy sections around it`) and all four fail against the previous parser; `.github/workflows/links.yml` already ran them ahead of lychee, and missed the defect only because every earlier test described a report that has an errors section. The real report from run 32454084765 is kept as a fixture and replayed by `experiments/issue-1021-link-checker-false-positive/reproduce.mjs`. What stays a finding rather than a change: the job still fails whenever lychee exits non-zero, so a lone runner-side timeout reds the gate over a healthy link, and making that non-fatal would be moving a limit. See finding 32. `rust/tests/web/issue-1021-link-checker.test.mjs` replays the committed report of run 32454084765 through `extractBrokenUrls` and holds it to the one link that timed out. |

An Anthropic-compatible surface answers it too, so `rust/src/server.rs` serves both spellings and `matrix_assert_proxy_ok` is left alone -- the same fix issue #671 made for the bare base path, for the same reason. `rust/tests/integration/issue_1021_client_preflight.rs` pins all three probes and was falsified against the unpatched server. | R1021-36 | A step that is terminated for running too long reports what made it slow. | Implemented: `scripts/run-with-budget-warning.sh` announces the failure, so it is what asks the question a reader asks next. This is the standing debug-output clause applied to CI: `Test (macos-15-intel / specification)` was terminated at its full 1200s budget still compiling dependencies, and the two candidate causes -- a slower runner, a colder compiler cache -- leave the same trace in the log, because cargo prints `Running \`sccache rustc ...\`` on a hit exactly as it does on a miss. Narrowing them took reconstructing per-crate rustc timestamps out of a megabyte of raw job log, and even that only ruled out a *partial* cache difference rather than closing the question, because the counters that would close it were never printed. The budget itself was not moved. See finding 34. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/ci-cd/issue_1021.rs`. |
| R1021-37 | A name is part of the interface, and a static analyser reads it as one. | Implemented: The `CodeQL` check reported 99 critical and high alerts on this branch, and every one of them was produced by an identifier's spelling. `rust/hard-coded-cryptographic-value` makes a sink of any argument reaching a parameter literally named `password`, `iv`, `nonce` or `salt`, so the `salt` parameter of `sample_index` -- an FNV-1a draw with no cryptography anywhere near it -- reported the 98 `temperature`, `guess_probability` and `questioning_rigor` literals that 24 files write into a `FormalizationSelectionConfig`; `rust/cleartext-logging` reads `session.?(id|key)` as account information, so `rust/src/cli_improve.rs` printing FNV-1a digests out of a binding called `session_id` reported as a leaked session token. The values are renamed after what they are (`seed`, `agent_session_digests`) with every seed string and every digest byte-identical before and after, and `rust/tests/unit/ci-cd/codeql_sink_heuristics.rs` holds both heuristics over every Rust file CodeQL analyses rather than over the two sites that were caught -- the same file set, minus the prefixes `.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml` ignores, which `the_scan_skips_the_same_directories_the_codeql_config_ignores` keeps in step. What stays a finding rather than a change: the two `assert!` alerts in `rust/tests/unit/docs_requirements/issue_917.rs` and `_918.rs` are true positives over real Agent CLI session ids and are left open rather than spelled around or dismissed, and `salt`'s presence in the upstream sink list -- where `key` is already excluded as too false-positive prone -- is proposed as an upstream report rather than filed. See finding 36. |

## Issue #1138 Prerequisite Discovery

Missing tools become observable, consent-bounded prerequisite needs. The
contract is covered by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1138_prerequisite_need.rs` and
`rust/tests/unit/issue_1138_install_scope.rs`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |

| R1138-6-2 | The check command runs before any output is called observed; unobserved output is labelled in every supported language. | Covered by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1138_prerequisite_need.rs`. |

## Issue #1138 Repository Workspace Protocol

Repository authoring uses one default-deny protocol, covered by
`rust/tests/unit/issue_1138_repository_workspace.rs` and
`rust/tests/unit/issue_1138_locate_targets.rs`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1138-3-1 | A repository task carries an origin and an exact base commit; a branch name is refused as a base. | Implemented by the repository-workspace request parser; covered by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1138_repository_workspace.rs`. |
| R1138-3-2 | Named targets are located by repository census or literal/path occurrence; ambiguity resolves to no target. | Implemented by `rust/src/repository_workspace/locate.rs`; covered by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1138_locate_targets.rs`. |
| R1138-3-3 | Named tests run and record command, exit code, and output before an obligation can be satisfied. | Implemented by the verification stage; covered by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1138_named_tests.rs` and `rust/tests/unit/issue_1138_repository_workspace.rs`. |
| R1138-3-4 | The offered patch is a unified diff computed from the tree and verified against the exact base. | Implemented by the workspace outcome; covered by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1138_repository_workspace.rs`. |
| R1138-3-5 | SWE-bench, the coding ladder, and self-authoring consume the same protocol document. | Partial (JS-first parity): Rust delivers it, while the JS twin has the document parser, the editor rule and the trace renderer but not the runners. `data/meta/repository-workspace-protocol.lino` is the one stage list of all three callers. It declares nine stages (clone, locate, read, serve, edit, session, verify, diff, commit), each with an `editor`: `any`, or `agent_session` for spawning `formal-ai serve` and harvesting the Agent CLI session id, which are data rather than a branch in code. SWE-bench (`external_benchmarks::solve_repository_case`) and the coding ladder (`formal-ai solve --task`) run it through `WorkspaceProtocol::execute`; self-authoring (`formal-ai solve --produces`, behind `scripts/author-change-with-formal-ai.sh`) runs it through `authoring_loop::run_authoring_with`, which iterates the stages of the document instead of a separate loop. All three write the same `repository-protocol.lino` (`repository_workspace::trace::ProtocolTrace`), one stage line per declared stage with its status. Covered by `rust/tests/unit/ci-cd/protocol_callers.rs` (the three callers, run against one local repository with fake serve and Agent CLI executables, record identical stage names; a document without the serve stage spawns no server; the committed trace records the opened commit gate), `rust/tests/unit/specification/repository_workspace_protocol.rs`, `rust/tests/unit/issue_1138_repository_workspace.rs`, `rust/tests/unit/issue_848_coding_ladder.rs` and `rust/tests/web/issue-1138-protocol-trace.test.mjs`; the Rust tests are new in round 14 and run first in CI. Remaining parity gap: the JS twin `js/agentic/crate/repository_workspace.mjs` ports the document parser, the editor rule and the trace renderer only; the protocol runners (`execute` and the authoring loop) have no JavaScript twin. |
| R1138-3-6 | Commands are default-deny and allowed by program, subcommand, and argument shape from seed data. | Implemented by the repository command allowlist; covered by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1138_command_allowlist.rs`. |
| R1138-3-7 | Authoring refuses commits by default; an allowed commit carries all self-hosting trailers and exact model evidence. | Implemented by `run_solve`, which is default-deny, and the authoring wrapper `scripts/author-change-with-formal-ai.sh`, reduced to that entry point, which passes `--commit` only when its caller asks (the self-authoring action does); the produced commit payload passes the canonical attribution parser. Covered by `rust/tests/unit/ci-cd/issue_1069.rs` (`the_authoring_wrapper_commits_only_when_asked`), `rust/tests/unit/issue_1138_solve_cli.rs` and `rust/tests/unit/specification/self_hosting_metric/solve_attribution.rs`. |
| R1138-3-8 | A missing prerequisite remains an evidenced unsatisfied need, never a pass or skip. | Implemented by the protocol outcome ledger; covered by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1138_repository_workspace.rs`. |
| R1138-3-9 | The protocol document is forgettable and regenerates to the same content id. | Covered by `rust/tests/unit/specification/repository_workspace_protocol.rs`. |
